note: doc 06 section 2.5. Structural rotations (who changes job), distinct from the movement patterns already seeded as library_items R1, R12 and R13. Every row states its cost in `risk`: a rotation library that lists only benefits is marketing, not coaching, so the validator refuses a row without one. Slot names in what_moves_json and animation_spec_json are the rotation's own generic names, not formation slot ids, because one rotation applies across several formations whose slot vocabularies differ.

items.name: Inverted fullback into the pivot
items.trigger: A goal kick, or centre-back circulation against a two-striker press.
coaching_points_json: The fullback steps inside while the ball is travelling, not once it has arrived, so the pivot line is already a two when the receiver looks up.
The winger ahead of him now holds that touchline alone, and has to stay high and wide to keep their fullback pinned.
The far fullback tucks in at the same moment: a back three that forms late is a back two for the first three seconds.
items.risk: The flank behind him is empty on the turnover, so this needs a winger who defends or a wide centre back who can cover the channel.

steps.caption: The centre back carries out and the first line comes to meet him.
The fullback steps inside beside the six while the far fullback tucks into the back line.
The pivot is a two, so the free man receives on the half-turn.

items.exemplar_note: Philipp Lahm under Guardiola at Bayern, Oleksandr Zinchenko at Arsenal. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Fullback into the eight line
items.trigger: Their block is already pinned deep and we need another body between the lines.
coaching_points_json: He arrives at the height of the eights, not between them and the ball, so he is a receiver rather than another circulator.
The single screener has to sit centrally and hold: the moment he chases the ball there is nobody behind six players.
items.risk: Only one screener sits behind six attacking players, so this is a shape for chasing a game, not a default setting.

steps.caption: The block is already deep, so circulation in front of it achieves nothing.
The fullback steps inside and forward to the height of the eights.
Six players now occupy the last two lines, with one screener behind them.

items.exemplar_note: Arsenal under Arteta with Zinchenko or Timber stepping high. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Centre back steps into midfield
items.trigger: Their first line refuses to press, so the free man has to come from the back.
coaching_points_json: He carries into the space rather than passing into it: the point is to make a defender decide, and a pass decides nothing.
The moment a midfielder comes to him, the pass is already gone into the space that midfielder left.
The remaining defenders slide across as he goes, so the line stays a line rather than becoming a gap.
items.risk: If he is caught stepping, the back line is a two against their front two with nobody spare behind it.

steps.caption: Their striker holds his position and refuses to press the ball.
The centre back carries past him into the pivot line.
Their midfield now has to come out, and the pass goes behind whoever does.

items.exemplar_note: John Stones for Manchester City, Josko Gvardiol carrying from the left. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Middle centre back of a three inverts
items.trigger: The keeper is under pressure and needs a bounce option that does not exist out wide.
coaching_points_json: He steps in front of the other two, not between them: the whole value is being a forward-facing option the keeper can see.
The two remaining defenders widen as he leaves, so the keeper still has two angles rather than one.
items.risk: It gives up the spare central defender against a lone striker who plays on the shoulder of the last man.

steps.caption: The keeper has the ball and both wide options are covered.
The middle defender steps in front of the other two.
The bounce goes through the centre, where nobody expected an option.

items.exemplar_note: Ruben Amorim's Sporting sides, with the central defender of the three stepping in. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Salida lavolpiana, the pivot drops in
items.trigger: Two strikers are pressing our two centre backs and we need a third builder.
coaching_points_json: The centre backs split as he drops, in the same movement: three players arriving at three places at once is what beats a front two.
He drops to receive facing forward. Dropping to stand with his back to play just moves the problem ten metres.
Somebody has to take the screening job he vacated, and the team should know who before the ball moves.
items.risk: It removes the screen in front of the back line, and played badly the counter goes straight through the space he left.

steps.caption: Two strikers press the pair, so there is no free man in the first line.
The six drops between the centre backs as they split.
Three against two, and the ball goes to whichever of the three is free.

items.exemplar_note: Named for Ricardo La Volpe, later a Guardiola staple with Busquets. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: One of the double pivot drops, the other holds
items.trigger: The press arrives in a 4-4-2 and our two centre backs are two against two.
coaching_points_json: Which pivot drops is decided by the ball, not by the team sheet: whichever one is on the far side of the press has the cleaner journey.
The partner slides central rather than staying wide, because he is now the only screen and has to cover the middle.
items.risk: The remaining pivot is alone against their two eights, so every second ball in the centre starts as a one against two.

steps.caption: Their front two splits our two centre backs and there is no spare man.
One pivot drops between them, the other slides across to screen alone.
The back three plays around the front two while the single screen holds.

items.exemplar_note: Liverpool under Slot, and Cesc Fabregas's Como. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: One wing back high, one deep
items.trigger: We are building down one side against a back four.
coaching_points_json: The ball-far wing back drops as the ball travels away from him, so the back four exists before the switch is even considered.
The near wing back stays on the touchline and does not come to the ball: he is the width, and width that moves inside is not width.
items.risk: The deep wing back is the only cover on his entire flank, so a switch away from the ball finds him alone against two.

steps.caption: We build down the right and the ball is travelling away from the left.
The far wing back drops into the back line, the near one holds the last line.
Four build the play, five occupy the last line, and one flank is covered by one player.

items.exemplar_note: Simone Inzaghi's Inter, with Dimarco high and Darmian tucked in. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Winger inside, fullback outside
items.trigger: Their fullback is tucking narrow to protect the centre back.
coaching_points_json: They swap in one movement, not one after the other, so their fullback never gets a moment with nobody to track.
The winger's first look from the half-space is the pass in behind, because that is the option he did not have on the touchline.
items.risk: The winger is no longer isolated in a one against one, so a qualitative superiority is traded for a positional one. Know which one you wanted.

steps.caption: Their fullback has tucked in narrow, so the touchline is unguarded.
The winger comes into the half-space as the fullback runs outside him.
The ball goes to whichever of the two their fullback did not follow.

items.name: Nine drops, wingers dive the channels
items.trigger: The ball reaches a midfielder who is facing forward.
coaching_points_json: The wingers go the instant he drops, not once he has the ball: the runs are what make the drop a problem.
This is the same movement the False-9 Drop and Wing Dive card animates, seeded here as a structural change rather than a one-off pattern.
items.risk: Nobody occupies the centre backs, so if the runs do not go the last line has no pin on it at all.

steps.caption: The midfielder receives facing forward, which is the only trigger needed.
The nine drops between the lines and both wingers dive the channels.
Their centre back either follows and opens the channel, or lets him turn.

items.exemplar_note: Lionel Messi under Guardiola, Roberto Firmino at Liverpool. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Two forwards drop to form the box midfield
items.trigger: We are winning the centre and want to keep it.
coaching_points_json: The two who drop take the half-spaces, not the centre: a box with a flat top is two players marked by one.
The wing backs must already be high when the box forms, or the shape has four central players and no width at all.
items.risk: The wide zones are empty except for the wing backs, and two exhausted wing backs is a real cost by the last twenty minutes.

steps.caption: The double pivot has the ball and their midfield is even with ours.
Both wide forwards drop into the half-spaces above the pivot.
Four central players in a box means the carrier always has two forward passes.

items.exemplar_note: Xabi Alonso's Leverkusen, and Manchester City's box seasons. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Hold the ball dead to invite the presser
items.trigger: Their first line is hesitating on the edge of pressing.
coaching_points_json: The sole of the foot on the ball, head up, body open. A ball that is still keeps every passing lane open at once.
The backward pass here is a trigger, not a retreat, and the whole team should move forward when it is played rather than back.
Rehearse the three exits before you rehearse the bait, because the bait without the exit is just a mistake with better posture.
items.risk: It is a genuine risk taken on purpose in our own third, so run it only with players who can execute under pressure, and tell them that plainly.

steps.caption: Their striker hesitates on the edge of pressing, so the ball stops dead.
The presser commits, and the pivot shows into the space he has left.
One pass past the first line puts us in a five against four beyond it.

items.exemplar_note: Roberto De Zerbi's Brighton. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Keeper as the spare man in the build
items.trigger: The opponent presses with one more player than we are building with.
coaching_points_json: He steps to the edge of the box and stays there: a keeper who drifts is neither a builder nor a goalkeeper.
He is the apex of the first-line rondo, so his job is to make the extra presser wrong, not to hit the longest pass available.
Agree the bail-out before the session starts. Every player should know which ball he is allowed to put out of play.
items.risk: Everything behind the keeper is empty, which makes this the single highest consequence rotation in the book.

steps.caption: They press with three against our two centre backs and the pivot.
The keeper steps to the edge of the box and the defenders widen.
Four against three in the first line, and the free man is always one pass away.

items.exemplar_note: Ederson at Manchester City, Manuel Neuer at Bayern. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Ten drops beside the pivot
items.trigger: Their ten or striker is screening our pivot and we cannot get out.
coaching_points_json: He drops to the side of the screen, not behind it, so the pass to him does not have to travel through the player causing the problem.
Somebody has to replace him between the lines within a few seconds, usually a winger coming inside, or we have simply run away from the space.
items.risk: We surrender the player between the lines, which is the whole point of the shape, so this is a temporary fix and never a setting.

steps.caption: Their ten stands on our pivot and the ball cannot leave the first line.
Our ten drops beside the pivot to make a midfield three.
The three plays out, and a winger comes inside to replace him between the lines.

items.name: Overload one side, switch to the isolated winger
items.trigger: We have a winger who wins his one against one.
coaching_points_json: The far winger stays wide and does nothing, which is the hardest instruction in the game to follow for ninety minutes.
The switch is prepared by a player who can see it before he receives, which usually means the ball goes backward once first.
items.risk: The switch has to be prepared rather than hopeful, because an unprepared long diagonal is a turnover inside our own build shape.

steps.caption: Six or seven players commit to the right side and their block slides across.
The overload holds the ball while the far winger simply stays wide.
The ball goes back to the pivot, then across, and the winger is one against one.
